name: terraform-awss-processing-module-refactor
instr:
The Terraform for our AWSS production processing platform in `/workspace/infra` has grown into one flat root module: everything is declared at the top level, its storage bucket roles, queue pipelines and ECS workload sizes are `count`-indexed by historical list position, and names, settings and tags are hard-coded throughout. Split it into four local modules (storage, messaging, compute and api) without touching the running infrastructure: against the current state, the plan has to come out as nothing but moves. As the one exception to the child-module file-path rule below, preserve the two existing `aws_lambda_function.filename` values exactly as the root-relative `zip/runEcsTask.zip` and `zip/urlSigner.zip`: those provider-visible strings are part of the recorded state, so the compute module's archive data sources write the generated ZIPs to the matching `${path.root}/zip/...` paths even though their source files remain under `${path.module}/src/...`. This exception applies only to those Lambda `filename` and archive `output_path` arguments.

There is no AWS access from this machine. `terraform init` works offline from the local provider mirror, `terraform.tfstate` is a copy of the production state, and `scripts/ci-plan.sh` runs what CI runs: a `terraform plan -refresh=false` against the state followed by the guardrail policies in `policies/`.

## Detailed Constraints

**How CI judges the change.** CI takes the repository alone and plans it with `terraform plan -refresh=fal
